name: Neon
blurb: Neon's only NMR-active stable isotope is 21Ne, 0.27 percent abundant with I = 3/2 and a receptivity of 6.7e-6 relative to 1H. It is never imaged, but 21Ne is spin-exchange optically pumped in K-Rb-21Ne comagnetometers, where its very long spin coherence makes it a rotation sensor.
mrNotes: 21Ne receptivity is about 1/26 of 13C, so thermal-equilibrium in vivo detection is not on the table at any field.
SEOP-polarized 21Ne is used in nuclear spin gyroscopes and self-compensating comagnetometers, not in imaging; there is no inhaled-neon MRI literature comparable to 3He, 83Kr or 129Xe.
20Ne and 22Ne, which make up 99.7 percent of natural neon, are even-even and spin 0.

isotopes.notes: Only NMR-active stable Ne isotope. Negative gamma, I = 3/2. Q = +10.155 fm2 (Pyykko); Stone's compilation lists +10.3(8) fm2 from the same atomic-beam work.

name: Sodium
blurb: 23Na is the second nucleus of clinical MRI: 100 percent abundant, spin 3/2, and 9.3 percent as receptive as 1H, which is enough for whole-brain tissue sodium maps in 10 to 20 minutes at 3T or 7T. Tissue sodium concentration rises in tumours, acute stroke, multiple sclerosis lesions and degenerating cartilage.
mrNotes: Larmor frequency 33.8 MHz at 3T and 78.9 MHz at 7T; needs a dedicated coil, a broadband transmit chain and usually a dual-tuned 23Na/1H setup for anatomical registration.

Relaxation is biexponential in tissue: T2* fast component roughly 0.5 to 5 ms and slow component 15 to 30 ms, so UTE, density-adapted radial or twisted-projection readouts with TE under 0.5 ms are mandatory.
T1 is short, about 15 to 40 ms, so TR can be 100 ms or less and thousands of averages are practical inside a clinical slot.
Tissue sodium runs about 10 to 45 mM against 140 mM in CSF and blood; in cartilage the 23Na signal tracks fixed charge density and therefore glycosaminoglycan content.

isotopes.shiftRange: -60 to +15 for Na compounds (sodide near -60); biological Na+ within a few ppm of 0
isotopes.notes: The in vivo X-nucleus after 1H. Triple-quantum filtering can weight the signal toward slow-motion (intracellular and bound) sodium at a large SNR cost.

name: Magnesium
blurb: 25Mg is 10 percent abundant with I = 5/2, but its receptivity is 2.7e-4 of 1H and free intracellular Mg2+ is only a few tenths of a millimolar, so it has never been seen in vivo. Magnesium reaches MR practice through bioresorbable alloy implants and, indirectly, through the 31P ATP chemical shift.
mrNotes: Free intracellular [Mg2+] in vivo is measured from the 31P alpha-to-beta ATP chemical shift difference, not from 25Mg.
25Mg solution and solid-state NMR needs 14 T or more; outside high-symmetry sites the quadrupolar coupling broadens lines badly.
Bioresorbable Mg alloy screws and pins are non-ferromagnetic, but they distort B0 locally and generate hydrogen gas pockets as they corrode, so the artifact changes shape over weeks.

isotopes.shiftRange: -15 to +25 for most Mg(II); the full diamagnetic range approaches 200 ppm
isotopes.notes: Negative gamma, I = 5/2, Q = +19.94 fm2. Receptivity 1.6 times 13C, but biological Mg2+ concentrations are far too low for in vivo work.

name: Aluminium
blurb: Aluminium is hardware, not signal: gradient coil formers, RF screens, cryostat outer vacuum vessels and service structures. 27Al itself is one of the most receptive quadrupolar nuclei known, 0.21 relative to 1H, but tissue aluminium is a trace element at micromolar levels so there is nothing to detect in vivo.
mrNotes: 27Al is routine in zeolite, cement and alumina solid-state NMR; the isotropic shift cleanly separates 4-, 5- and 6-coordinate aluminium.

Aluminium is non-ferromagnetic but very conductive. Moving a large Al object quickly through the fringe field induces eddy currents and a real braking force, and Al near the imaging volume both loads RF coils and supports gradient-switching eddy currents.
RF skin depth in aluminium is about 7 micrometres at 128 MHz, so thin sheet or foil is an adequate RF screen; the same conductivity is what makes it a poor choice close to gradients unless slotted.
Ti-6Al-4V, the common implant alloy, is 6 percent aluminium by weight, but its MR artifact is governed by titanium's susceptibility.

isotopes.shiftRange: -50 to +300 (AlO6 near 0, AlO5 near +35, AlO4 +55 to +80)
isotopes.notes: 100 percent abundant, DP 0.21 of 1H, the most receptive quadrupolar nucleus in this slice. Q = +14.66 fm2 is the Pyykko recommended value; a 2019 redetermination proposes +14.82 fm2.

name: Silicon
blurb: 29Si is spin 1/2, 4.7 percent abundant, with a negative gyromagnetic ratio. Its in vivo relevance is hyperpolarized silicon particles: DNP-polarized 29Si in a particle core keeps T1 of tens of minutes, long enough to inject and then image, which no 13C agent can do. Silicon otherwise appears in MR as silicone implants read out on 1H.
mrNotes: DNP-hyperpolarized silicon microparticles have been imaged in live mice with an in vivo 29Si T1 near 40 min, versus roughly 60 s for hyperpolarized 13C pyruvate.
Polarization is transferred from surface dangling-bond electrons into the particle core, and no chemical-shift information survives, so the particle behaves as a pure positive-contrast tracer.

Silicone (PDMS) in breast implants resonates roughly 4.5 ppm upfield of water and is imaged with silicone-selective or water- and fat-suppressed 1H sequences; this is a 1H measurement, not a 29Si one.
29Si has a negative gamma, which reverses the sense of the rotating-frame phase relative to 1H on the same hardware.

isotopes.shiftRange: -400 to +50 (TMS 0; Q4 silicate framework sites -100 to -120)
isotopes.notes: Spin 1/2 with negative gamma, so NOE from 1H is negative and INEPT or DEPT transfer is the usual route in chemistry. In vivo only as hyperpolarized particles.

name: Phosphorus
blurb: 31P is the workhorse of in vivo metabolic MRS: 100 percent abundant, spin 1/2, no quadrupole, and 6.7 percent of 1H receptivity. One spectrum gives PCr, the three ATP resonances, inorganic phosphate, phosphomono- and phosphodiesters, and from chemical shifts alone both intracellular pH and free Mg2+.
mrNotes: PCr defines 0 ppm in vivo. The Pi-to-PCr shift gives intracellular pH through a titration curve with pKa near 6.75, and the alpha-to-beta ATP shift difference gives free [Mg2+].
T1 is long, roughly 3 to 6 s for PCr at 3T, so acquisition is TR-limited; Ernst-angle excitation, broadband 1H decoupling and NOE are used to claw back SNR.
Larmor frequency 51.8 MHz at 3T and 120.8 MHz at 7T; 31P benefits strongly from 7T, where the 30 ppm metabolite spread becomes 3.6 kHz and PDE and PME separate cleanly.
Muscle PCr is about 30 mM and brain PCr about 4 mM, so muscle 31P-MRS resolves exercise recovery kinetics in seconds while brain work needs minutes per voxel.

Red phosphorus, which is what CRC's -20.77e-6 cm3/mol names. White phosphorus, the thermochemical reference state, is -26.66e-6, 28 percent larger in magnitude; both are quoted per mole of P atoms, not per mole of P4.

isotopes.shiftRange: -25 to +25 in vivo (PCr 0, Pi +4.9, beta-ATP -16.3); about -250 to +250 in chemistry
isotopes.notes: The best non-proton in vivo nucleus: spin 1/2, 100 percent abundant, a 30 ppm in vivo spread with no overlapping water line to suppress.

name: Sulfur
blurb: 33S is the only NMR-active sulfur isotope: I = 3/2, 0.76 percent abundant, receptivity 1.7e-5 of 1H, and quadrupole-broadened in everything except highly symmetric sites such as sulfate. It has never been observed in vivo and is unlikely to be.
mrNotes: Even in solution, 33S lines run to tens of kHz away from tetrahedral symmetry: sulfate and CS2 are observable, DMSO effectively is not.

Sulfur reaches MR through its compounds rather than its nucleus: SF6 is one of the inhaled 19F gases used for lung ventilation imaging, and sulfate groups on glycosaminoglycans set the fixed charge density that 23Na cartilage imaging reports.

isotopes.shiftRange: roughly -100 to +400 (SO4 2- at 0, SO2 near +375); metal sulfides span over 600 ppm
isotopes.notes: Receptivity 0.10 relative to 13C. Q = -6.94 fm2 is Pyykko's 2017 molecular value from CS and SiS; older IUPAC tables carry -6.78 fm2.

name: Chlorine
blurb: 35Cl MRI has been demonstrated in human brain and muscle at 7T, giving a direct readout of tissue chloride, the counter-ion whose distribution reports cell volume regulation, oedema and tumour biology. It is roughly an order of magnitude harder than sodium, so it stays confined to ultra-high-field research sites.
mrNotes: 35Cl receptivity is 3.6e-3 of 1H, about 1/26 of 23Na, and tissue chloride is lower than tissue sodium, so at matched resolution 35Cl SNR is far worse than 23Na.
Larmor frequency 29.2 MHz at 7T; short T2* forces UTE or density-adapted radial readout, the same machinery as sodium imaging.

35Cl is always the choice over 37Cl: 3.1 times more abundant and 5.4 times more receptive. Its quadrupole moment is the larger of the two, -8.165 against -6.435 fm2, so 35Cl lines are about 1.6 times broader; the receptivity wins anyway.
Chloride sits near 110 mM extracellularly and roughly 5 to 30 mM inside cells, so a 35Cl image is heavily extracellular-weighted, the opposite bias to 39K.

isotopes.shiftRange: aqueous Cl- near 0; overall range about 1000 ppm, with ClO4- at the high-frequency end
isotopes.notes: The practical chlorine nucleus. Imaged in human brain and muscle at 7T; also the standard nucleus for chloride-binding studies by quadrupolar relaxation.
Chemically identical shifts to 35Cl but 5.4 times less receptive; used mainly to confirm that a broad line is really chlorine, since quadrupolar linewidths scale as Q squared.

name: Argon
blurb: Argon has no NMR-active naturally occurring isotope: 36Ar, 38Ar and 40Ar are all even-even with I = 0. Along with cerium it is the standard example of an element that is completely MR-silent.
mrNotes: This is why the hyperpolarized noble-gas family is 3He, 83Kr and 129Xe and stops there; argon offers no spin to polarize.
Argon is used as an inert purge and cover gas during magnet service and in optical-pumping cell fabrication, where being MR-silent and weakly diamagnetic is an advantage.
The spin-active argon isotopes, 39Ar at 269 y and 37Ar at 35 d, exist only at trace cosmogenic levels and have no MR or nuclear-medicine use.

name: Potassium
blurb: 39K MRI has been shown in human muscle and brain at 7T in about 30 min. Potassium is the dominant intracellular cation, near 150 mM inside cells against 4 mM outside, so a 39K image is intrinsically intracellular-weighted, but gamma is only 1.99 MHz/T and most of the signal decays inside the readout dead time.
mrNotes: Larmor frequency 13.9 MHz at 7T, low enough that coil Q, preamplifier noise figure and sample loading, rather than the spins, often set the achievable SNR.
39K receptivity is 4.8e-4 of 1H, about 1/195 of 23Na; combined with short T2* this puts practical in vivo resolution in the centimetre range.
Potassium vapour is the pump partner in hybrid K-Rb spin-exchange optical pumping for 3He, and in K-Rb-21Ne comagnetometers.
40K is the naturally radioactive potassium isotope, 0.0117 percent at 1.25e9 y; it is the dominant internal gamma source in whole-body counting but is irrelevant to MR.

isotopes.shiftRange: aqueous K+ within a few ppm of 0; solid salts span over 100 ppm (solid KCl at +47.8)
isotopes.notes: The only practical potassium nucleus for imaging. Demonstrated in human muscle and brain at 7T with roughly 30 min acquisitions.
84 times less receptive than 39K and with a larger quadrupole moment, so it is never the in vivo choice; useful only to confirm quadrupolar assignments.
Naturally occurring long-lived radioisotope with the unusual spin I = 4 and a negative moment. Receptivity 6.1e-7 of 1H; of interest to nuclear physics and whole-body counting, not to MR.
